chunks: Indeed, Allah, the Blessed and Exalted, did not grant people freedom of choice in their actions to choose between good and evil; rather, He gave them will and ability, and made good and evil in their actions, and gave them knowledge of good and evil, and gave them the ability to act upon them, and established the proof upon themselves.
ai.seo_question: What is the Shia view on human free will and divine decree?
ai.summary: In *Kamal al-Din*, Shaykh al-Saduq articulates the Shia doctrine of *Al-Amal bayn al-Amrayn* (the position between the two extremes), reconciling divine omnipotence with human accountability by asserting that God creates the capacity (*qudrah*) and will (*iradah*) for the servant, who then acquires the action through free choice. This nuanced view, championed by the Imams, refutes both the Jabriyyah (determinists) and the Qadariyyah (absolute free will proponents), establishing that human agency is a created attribute that enables moral responsibility without compromising God's ultimate sovereignty.
